input.explanation:
The fault: deploy/values-production.yaml sets `metrics.portName: http-metrics` (changed in 9f4ad14). deploy/scrape.yaml, the ServiceMonitor, still picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`. Its own comment says it picks by name, that the two names must match, and that nothing checks this: a name that matches no port gives an empty target list, not an error. So when the rename went out, the shop kept serving, but Prometheus had nothing left to scrape.

The fix: change `endpoints[0].port` in deploy/scrape.yaml to `http-metrics`, matching the value now in production. This keeps the deploy that renamed the port instead of reverting it. Rolling the values back to `metrics` without this change would just leave the same trap for the next rename.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py reads both files from the repository root. It takes `portName` from the `metrics:` block of values-production.yaml and every `port:` under `endpoints:` in scrape.yaml, and asserts that each endpoint's port equals portName. It uses plain text parsing, so it adds no YAML library dependency. Against the files as they stood before this change, it is written to fail (`metrics` vs `http-metrics`). It turns the agreement the comment says nothing enforces into something CI checks, so the next rename that changes only one file fails a test instead of breaking the metrics silently.

# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# The ServiceMonitor the platform applies with the shop's chart, kept in the
# repository beside how the shop is deployed, so that how it is collected
# changes in the same pull request as what it is collected from.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. A name that matches no port is not an error to the operator,
# it is a target list with nothing in it - so tests/io_shop/test_scrape_config.py
# checks that the two agree.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s

input.summary: Point the ServiceMonitor at the renamed http-metrics port, and test that it matches metrics.portName
